experimentos.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
experimentos.headline: When does a burning fuel droplet go out?
experimentos.summary: FLEX ignited single droplets of methanol and heptane, free-floating or held on a thin fiber, inside the Combustion Integrated Rack of the International Space Station. Oxygen, pressure and the suppressant gases CO2 and helium were varied to map when a flame survives and when it goes out, including the Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI): the lowest oxygen that still supports a flame.
experimentos.why_it_matters: It measures how much oxygen a fuel fire needs and how well CO2 or helium put it out in microgravity, a direct input for designing fire suppression on spacecraft.

readiness.reason: 274 tests, each with its conditions and numeric results (burning rate, burn time, extinction diameter) plus how the flame ended.

experimentos.tests_note: 274 droplet tests in the PSI experimental table.

Chamber pressure (760 mmHg = 1 atm)

variables.col: O initial ambient composition; mole fraction
variables.meaning: Oxygen (O2) fraction at the start (0.21 = air)

variables.col: N initial ambient composition; mole fraction
variables.meaning: Nitrogen (N2) fraction at the start

variables.col: CO initial ambient composition; mole fraction
variables.meaning: CO2 fraction at the start (suppressant). The header lost the '2'; the TestSheets call it CO2 Mole Fraction

variables.col: He initial ambient composition; mole fraction
variables.meaning: Helium fraction at the start (suppressant)
Droplet size at ignition (D0)
How the flame ended: Extinction, Disruption (droplet broke apart) or Completion (burned out)
Burning-rate constant K from the d² law. The header says mm, but the TestSheets give kavg in mm²/s
How long the flame lasted
Droplet size when the visible flame went out (Dext); empty if it burned out or broke apart

variables.col: FLEX Test #, FLEX Identifier, Test Date, Test GMT

data_notes: Open the CSV with encoding latin-1.
Fiber (yes/no) and gas temperature are only in the 272 TestSheet files, not in the table.
Burn time is roughly D0²/K by physics: do not use one output to predict another.

experimentos.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids II
experimentos.headline: How do real spacecraft materials burn in slow airflow?
experimentos.summary: BASS-II burned solid materials (PMMA acrylic films, slabs and rods, SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric, Nomex and a candle) in a small wind tunnel inside the ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox. Airflow (up to 40 cm/s) and oxygen (lowered below 21 % by adding nitrogen) were varied to study ignition, flame growth, spread and extinction in opposed and concurrent flow.
experimentos.why_it_matters: It tests whether NASA's Earth-based upward-burning material test (NASA-STD-6001 Test 1) is really the worst case for fires in space.

readiness.reason: 129 tests with gas measurements before and after each burn (O2, CO2, CO); whether the flame went out is only written in the report's appendix.

experimentos.tests_note: 129 tests in the PSI experimental table.

Air speed in the duct; several values mean it was changed during the test
Oxygen at the start, calibrated with the ISS air analyzer (MCA)
Carbon dioxide at the start
Carbon monoxide at the start
Oxygen at the end (initial minus final = oxygen consumed by the fire)
Carbon dioxide at the end
Carbon monoxide at the end, a toxic gas ('OR' = over range, above 1000 ppm)
The Summary Report computes it from the oxygen consumed: 13.1 kJ per gram of O2
Test code (PI initial + number), date, day of year, sample number

Ignition, spread and extinction notes are in Appendix A of the BASS-II Summary Report, not in the CSV.

experimentos.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids
experimentos.headline: Can a nitrogen jet put out a fire on board?
experimentos.summary: The first BASS campaign compared how realistic, thicker fuels burn in microgravity with NASA's Earth-based material test, and checked whether a jet of nitrogen, an inert suppressant similar to the one used on the ISS, can put the flames out. Samples included SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric, PMMA spheres and slabs, wax, candles and Nomex, burned in opposed and concurrent airflow.
experimentos.why_it_matters: It links material flammability in space to the tests used on Earth and checks an inert-gas way to put out fires in a crewed vehicle.

readiness.reason: 122 tests; the CSV only has dates and materials. Conditions are in the As Run Test Matrix spreadsheet and results are free-text observations.

experimentos.tests_note: 122 rows in the PSI experimental table.

variables.meaning: Material and size (e.g. SIBAL 2 cm, PMMA sphere 1 cm)
Air inlet plate: 0 = most flow, 2 = least
Air speed; adjustable from 5 to 50 cm/s according to the SRD
Nitrogen suppressant flow (0 to 500 cc/min according to the SRD)
Cabin oxygen; stored as a fraction (0.221 = 22.1 %)

experimentos.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment 2
experimentos.headline: Droplets of real-world fuels and fuel mixtures
experimentos.summary: FLEX-2 extended FLEX to fuels and conditions closer to real engines: pure and two-component droplets of fuels such as decane, octane, heptane and iso-octane, two-droplet arrays and droplets moving through a slow flow. It was designed to give benchmark data on burning rate, flame extinction and soot formation to validate droplet combustion models.
experimentos.why_it_matters: Its benchmark data help validate the combustion models used to predict how liquid fuels burn and go out, in space and in engines on Earth.

readiness.reason: Its PSI table lists the test ranges (8 rows), not per-test results; per-test files hold gas mixtures, chamber readings and radiometer signals.

experimentos.tests_note: The PSI table has 8 rows of test ranges, not individual tests.

variables.meaning: Fuel or fuel mixture tested
Droplet size range at ignition
Gas around the droplet (O2/N2 or O2/He)
Oxygen levels tested

Slow flow imposed on the droplet
Flame radiation at 100 readings per second; flame duration could be computed from it

variables.col: (SRD) Burning rate, extinction diameter, soot shell
variables.meaning: What the experiment measures according to its Science Requirements Document; not tabulated

data_notes: For droplet models, use FLEX: same hardware, with results per test.

experimentos.name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment I
experimentos.headline: A large fire, safely, inside a cargo ship
experimentos.platform: Cygnus cargo vehicle (after leaving the ISS)
experimentos.summary: Saffire-I lit a large fire, a 94 × 40.6 cm sheet of SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric, inside the uncrewed Cygnus cargo vehicle after it left the ISS, so no crew was at risk. The flame spread with a 20 cm/s concurrent airflow while two cameras, thermocouples, radiometers, O2 and CO2 sensors, pressure sensors and anemometers recorded how the fire grew.
experimentos.why_it_matters: It shows how fast a realistic, large fire grows in microgravity, something too dangerous to test with a crew on board.

readiness.reason: Only 2 samples, but about 11,000 sensor readings per sample (temperatures, radiation, O2, CO2).

experimentos.tests_note: 2 samples; rows F1/F2 in the table are camera reference images, not tests.

Concurrent: the flame moves with the airflow; Opposed: against it

variables.meaning: Fire growth over time: gas levels, gas and sample temperatures, flame radiation

Sensor time series: Raw Data / Reduced Gravity / *Sensor*.xlsx, sheet Calibrated Data.

experimentos.name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment II
experimentos.headline: Nine materials: space flame vs. Earth test
experimentos.platform: Cygnus cargo vehicle (after leaving the ISS)
experimentos.summary: Saffire-II burned nine 5 × 29 cm samples (SIBAL fabric, silicone, flat and structured PMMA, and PMMA with Nomex) inside Cygnus, at 20 or 30 cm/s in concurrent or opposed flow. The samples have the same size as NASA's Earth flammability screening test, so their burn length and spread rate in microgravity can be compared with the same materials tested on the ground.
experimentos.why_it_matters: It checks whether materials approved with the 1-g screening test behave the same way in microgravity.

readiness.reason: 9 samples with microgravity vs. 1-g burn length and spread rate: good for comparison charts, too few to train a model.

experimentos.name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment III
experimentos.headline: The large fabric fire, with more wind
experimentos.platform: Cygnus cargo vehicle (after leaving the ISS)
experimentos.summary: Saffire-III repeated the large SIBAL fabric fire (94 × 40.6 cm) inside Cygnus at a faster 30 cm/s airflow, instead of the 20 cm/s of Saffire-I, with concurrent or opposed flow. Cameras, thermocouples, radiometers and O2, CO2 and pressure sensors recorded the fire.
experimentos.why_it_matters: Comparing it with Saffire-I shows how ventilation speed changes the growth of a large fire in microgravity.

readiness.reason: 2 samples; its table lists the setup only. The fire behaviour is in the sensor time series and images.
